diagnoses.primary_lay_explanation: Crohn's disease is a long‑term condition that makes the intestines inflamed. The patient had a serious belly infection (sepsis) because of this.

anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: Blood pressure was a little lower than normal, which can make you feel dizzy or faint.
Kidneys were not filtering waste well, so toxins can build up in the body.
There was infected fluid collecting inside the belly, which needed treatment.
The patient was breathing normally without needing extra oxygen.

procedures_performed.name: Ileocolectomy
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: Surgery to remove a damaged part of the intestine (the ileum and part of the colon).

procedures_performed.name: Creation of new anastomosis
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: The surgeon reconnected the healthy ends of the intestine after removing the damaged part.

procedures_performed.name: Ileostomy
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: An opening (stoma) was made in the belly wall to let waste exit into a bag outside the body while the intestine heals.

procedures_performed.name: Transfer to Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: Patient was moved to the ICU for close monitoring because of the serious infection.

medications.name: Ertapenem
medications.purpose_lay: Strong antibiotic injection to kill the bacteria causing the belly infection.
medications.timing_dosage: 1 gram per day, injected into muscle, for 4 weeks

medications.name: Vancomycin
medications.purpose_lay: Powerful antibiotic used against tough bacteria that other antibiotics cannot kill.

medications.name: Meropenem
medications.purpose_lay: Broad‑spectrum antibiotic to treat serious infections in the blood and belly.

medications.name: KCL 6% (Potassium Chloride)
medications.purpose_lay: Potassium supplement to keep normal potassium levels in the blood, which is important for heart function.

medications.name: Loperamide
medications.purpose_lay: Medicine to slow down bowel movements and reduce diarrhea or high ostomy output.

medications.name: Calcium Carbonate
medications.purpose_lay: Calcium supplement to keep bones strong and maintain calcium levels in the blood.

medications.name: Cholestyramine
medications.purpose_lay: Medicine that binds bile acids to help reduce diarrhea that can happen after intestine surgery.

medications.name: Muciloid
medications.purpose_lay: Fiber supplement to help regulate bowel movements and make stool more formed.

warning_signs_red_flags: Return of fever or chills (infection may be back)
Sudden drop in blood pressure, dizziness, or fainting
Severe belly pain or swelling
Decrease in ostomy output or no output for more than 6 hours
Blood in ostomy bag or dark/black coloured output
Reduced urine output (kidney problem getting worse)

appointments: Follow‑up appointment and planned hospitalization on 01/22
ongoing_treatments: Continue oral medications: Loperamide, Calcium Carbonate, Cholestyramine, Muciloid
lifestyle_diet_advice: Stay hydrated to support kidney function

diagnoses.primary_lay_explanation: A serious infection in the blood caused by a tough bacteria that is resistant to many medicines. It spread to the heart, spine and muscle.
secondary: Spondylodiscitis (infection of the L2‑L4 vertebrae and discs)
Mitral valve infective endocarditis (infection of the heart valve)
Ileopsoas muscle abscess (pus collection in the left thigh muscle)
Sacral pressure injury (skin sore on the lower back)
Arteriovenous fistula stenosis (narrowing of the fistula used for dialysis)

anomalies_detected.finding: Positive blood cultures for methicillin‑resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: The bacteria that caused the infection was found in the blood and it is a type that is hard to kill with many antibiotics.
The infection was cleared from the blood after treatment.

anomalies_detected.finding: Spondylodiscitis at L2‑L4 with epidural abscess
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: The lower spine bones and discs were infected and there was pus pressing on the spinal cord.

anomalies_detected.finding: Mitral valve vegetation (infection on the heart valve)
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: A small growth of infected material was seen on the heart valve.

anomalies_detected.finding: Left ileopsoas abscess 15 x 2.1 x 1.8 cm with edema
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: A pus collection in the left thigh muscle near the spine.

anomalies_detected.finding: Sacral pressure injury (skin sore on lower back)
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: A sore on the skin caused by staying in one position for too long.
The tube used for dialysis was narrowed, which can make dialysis less effective.

procedures_performed.name: Removal of femoral catheter
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: The tube that was used to give medicines and take blood was taken out to stop the infection.

procedures_performed.name: Surgical debridement of sacral pressure injury
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: The sore on the lower back was cleaned and the dead tissue was removed to help it heal.

procedures_performed.name: Hemodialysis sessions
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: Blood was filtered through a machine to replace kidney function.

procedures_performed.name: Attempted percutaneous abscess puncture
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A needle was tried to drain the pus from the thigh muscle but was not done because of nearby intestines.

medications.name: Vancomycin
medications.purpose_lay: Strong antibiotic that kills MRSA bacteria.
medications.timing_dosage: 0.5 g given after each hemodialysis session until 01/09/2021

warning_signs_red_flags: New or worsening fever
Increasing back pain or new pain in the chest or abdomen
Sudden weakness or numbness in limbs
Shortness of breath or chest pain
Signs of heart failure (rapid heartbeat, swelling in legs)
Any new or worsening skin sore that does not heal
Reduced urine output or sudden change in dialysis effectiveness

appointments: Phlebography of arteriovenous fistula – scheduled (date not set)

diagnoses.primary_lay_explanation: A lung infection caused by a bacteria that can spread through the air. The bacteria in this case can be killed by the medicine isoniazid.
secondary: Spontaneous pneumothorax (air in the chest cavity causing lung collapse)
Pleurostomy (surgical opening in the chest wall)
Exploratory thoracotomy (surgery to look inside the chest)
Hypovolemic shock (low blood volume after bleeding)
Right pneumonectomy (removal of the right lung)

symptoms_at_admission: Sudden pain in the right chest that spreads to the right neck

anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: Normal heart beat rate for an adult.
Blood has enough oxygen, which is normal.

anomalies_detected.finding: Auscultation: breath sounds absent on the right side, present on the left
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: The doctor could not hear breathing sounds on the right side because the lung is collapsed or filled with fluid.
The chest does not expand evenly on both sides, indicating a problem on the right side.
A low level of a marker that usually rises when there is a serious infection.

anomalies_detected.finding: Sputum bacilloscopy positive 10‑99 bacilli per 100 fields
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: The test found many tuberculosis bacteria in the cough sample.

anomalies_detected.finding: Sensitivity test: isoniazid sensitive, rifampin element present
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: The tuberculosis bacteria can be killed by the medicines isoniazid and rifampin.

anomalies_detected.finding: Surgical wound in good condition, dry, no dehiscence
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: The surgical scar looks healthy and is not opening up.

procedures_performed.name: Right chest drainage
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A tube was inserted into the chest to remove air or fluid from around the lungs.

procedures_performed.name: Pleurostomy
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A surgical opening was made in the chest wall to help drain fluid or air.

procedures_performed.name: Closure of pleurostomy
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: The surgical opening was closed after the chest was cleared.

procedures_performed.name: New pleurotomy
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: Another opening was made in the chest wall to drain fluid.

procedures_performed.name: Exploratory thoracotomy
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A surgical cut was made in the chest to look inside and treat bleeding.

procedures_performed.name: Packing of tuberculous cavity with compresses
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: The surgeon filled the infected cavity with gauze to stop bleeding.

procedures_performed.name: Right pneumonectomy by lateral thoracotomy
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: The entire right lung was removed through a side cut in the chest.

procedures_performed.name: Tracheostomy
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A small opening was made in the windpipe to help breathing after lung removal.

procedures_performed.name: Chest drain removal
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: The tube that drained fluid from the chest was taken out.

procedures_performed.name: Tracheostomy removal
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: The opening in the windpipe was closed after breathing was stable.

medications.name: Vancomycin
medications.purpose_lay: Strong antibiotic to kill tough bacteria that other medicines cannot kill.

medications.name: Meropenem
medications.purpose_lay: Broad‑spectrum antibiotic for serious infections.

medications.name: Amikacin
medications.purpose_lay: Antibiotic used for resistant bacterial infections.

medications.name: Rifampicin
medications.purpose_lay: Medicine that kills tuberculosis bacteria.
medications.timing_dosage: Continued as part of TB treatment (oral)

medications.name: Isoniazid
medications.purpose_lay: Medicine that kills tuberculosis bacteria.
medications.timing_dosage: Continued as part of TB treatment (oral)

medications.name: Oral iron replacement
medications.purpose_lay: Supplement to treat low iron levels and help make healthy blood.

warning_signs_red_flags: Sudden chest pain or swelling
Shortness of breath that gets worse quickly
Fever or chills that come back
Blood in cough or sputum
Sudden drop in oxygen level or feeling faint
Any new or worsening pain in the chest or abdomen

appointments: Follow‑up appointment at the organization (date not specified)
Follow‑up appointment with thoracic surgery team (date not specified)
ongoing_treatments: Continue oral rifampicin and isoniazid for tuberculosis
Continue any other TB medications as prescribed
lifestyle_diet_advice: Follow any dietary advice given by the team (not specified)

diagnoses.primary: Septic shock with multi‑organ failure leading to cardiorespiratory arrest
diagnoses.primary_lay_explanation: A severe infection that made the blood pressure drop and the heart stop working, causing the patient to die.
secondary: Fournier's gangrene (skin infection of the genital area)

symptoms_at_admission: Infection in the thigh and pubis
Skin infection in the genital area

anomalies_detected.finding: Septic shock with low blood pressure
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: Blood pressure was very low because the infection was spreading fast.
Heart was beating slower than normal.
Heart’s electrical signal was delayed, which can lead to serious rhythm problems.
Too much potassium in the blood, which can stop the heart.
The heart stopped beating and the patient could not breathe on their own.

procedures_performed.name: Drainage of thigh abscess (12/03)
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A tube was inserted to remove pus from the infected thigh.

procedures_performed.name: Drain placement (12/15)
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A drain was put in to keep pus from building up again.

procedures_performed.name: Incision in ICU (12/17)
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A surgical cut was made to remove infected tissue and drain pus.

procedures_performed.name: Dialysis via fistula (12/16)
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: Kidneys were helped by a machine that filters the blood through a fistula.

procedures_performed.name: Intubation and mechanical ventilation
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A tube was put into the airway to help the patient breathe.

procedures_performed.name: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) after arrest
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: Hands‑on chest compressions and rescue breaths were given to try to restart the heart.

procedures_performed.name: Electrical cardioversion
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A shock was delivered to the heart to try to restore a normal rhythm.

procedures_performed.name: Drainage of Fournier's gangrene
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: Infected tissue in the genital area was removed and drained.

medications.name: Dobutamine
medications.purpose_lay: Medicine to help the heart pump better during low blood pressure.

medications.name: Ceftriaxone
medications.purpose_lay: Strong antibiotic to kill the bacteria in the abscess.
medications.timing_dosage: Given after culture showed Escherichia coli

medications.name: Polymyxin D
medications.purpose_lay: Antibiotic for tough bacteria that other drugs cannot kill.

medications.name: Amikacin
medications.purpose_lay: Antibiotic to treat serious infections.

medications.name: Vancomycin
medications.purpose_lay: Strong antibiotic for resistant bacteria.

medications.name: Norepinephrine
medications.purpose_lay: Medicine to raise blood pressure during shock.

medications.name: Calcium gluconate
medications.purpose_lay: Medicine to lower dangerous potassium levels.

medications.name: Bicarbonate
medications.purpose_lay: Medicine to help balance blood acidity and lower potassium.

medications.name: Atropine
medications.purpose_lay: Medicine to try to stop slow heart rate.

warning_signs_red_flags: Sudden drop in blood pressure or fainting
Heart stops beating (cardiac arrest)
Very high potassium levels (hyperkalemia)
Severe infection spreading to the bloodstream (septic shock)
Uncontrolled bleeding or pus drainage

diagnoses.primary_lay_explanation: A viral infection that affects the lungs and can make breathing hard.

anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: The test showed the virus was present in the body.
The virus was no longer detected in the body.
Blood oxygen level was very low compared to the amount of oxygen given.

anomalies_detected.finding: Candidemia – blood and catheter tip cultures positive for Candida albicans on 06/23
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: Fungus was found in the blood, which can spread quickly.
Kidney function was fluctuating and at one point was higher than normal, indicating kidney injury.

anomalies_detected.finding: Hypokalemia (low potassium) resolved after magnesium replacement
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: Potassium levels were too low, which can affect heart and muscle function.

anomalies_detected.finding: Hypercapnia (high CO2) seen in blood gas analysis on 06/07
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: Too much carbon dioxide in the blood, meaning breathing was not clearing it well.
The patient was not fully alert and had a low level of consciousness.

anomalies_detected.finding: Blood pressure 132/80, heart rate 80, oxygen saturation 100% on 3.5 L/min via tracheostomy, respiratory rate 16
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: These vital signs were within normal limits.

anomalies_detected.finding: No signs of respiratory distress, no edema, normal pulses, capillary refill <3 sec
anomalies_detected.lay_explanation: The body was not showing signs of severe fluid or breathing problems at that time.

procedures_performed.name: Intubation and mechanical ventilation
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A tube was inserted into the airway to help the patient breathe.

procedures_performed.name: Extubation
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: The breathing tube was removed to allow the patient to breathe on their own.

procedures_performed.name: Reintubation
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: The breathing tube was put back in because the patient could not breathe well after extubation.

procedures_performed.name: Tracheostomy
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A surgical opening was made in the windpipe to allow easier breathing and suctioning.

procedures_performed.name: Cannula exchange for tracheostomy
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: The tube in the tracheostomy was replaced to keep the airway clear.

procedures_performed.name: Echocardiogram
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: An ultrasound of the heart to check for infections or problems.

procedures_performed.name: BIPAP therapy
procedures_performed.lay_explanation: A machine that helps the patient breathe by giving extra pressure during inhalation and exhalation.

medications.name: Micafungin
medications.purpose_lay: An antifungal medicine to treat the blood infection caused by Candida.

medications.name: Fluconazole
medications.purpose_lay: Another antifungal medicine used to treat the Candida infection.
medications.timing_dosage: Started on 06/30, dose increased to 200 mg every 8 hours after negative blood culture

medications.name: Furosemide
medications.purpose_lay: A diuretic (water pill) to help the kidneys remove excess fluid.

medications.name: Magnesium replacement
medications.purpose_lay: Supplement to correct low magnesium levels.

medications.name: Ceftriaxone
medications.purpose_lay: An antibiotic used to treat a urinary tract infection.

medications.name: Quetiapine
medications.purpose_lay: An antipsychotic medication that was stopped during the hospital stay.

warning_signs_red_flags: Sudden drop in oxygen saturation or breathing difficulty
New or worsening fever or chills
Increased redness, swelling, or pain around the tracheostomy site
Blood in the tracheostomy tube or sudden loss of breathing
Sudden increase in blood pressure or heart rate
New or worsening abdominal pain or distension
Signs of sepsis such as high temperature, rapid heart rate, or low blood pressure

ongoing_treatments: Continue fluconazole for 14 days after negative blood culture
lifestyle_diet_advice: Follow a balanced diet to support kidney health
